intro: Paste the inventory of unread signal sources, the single-question 30-day pilot, and the charter that binds it — followed by the 250–350 word write-up including your position on this module's claim. Resubmission is free and unlimited — the score is a mirror, not a gate.
activityContext:
You are grading a learner submission for AI 301 · The Specialist, Employee Experience / Internal Comms track. Module 7 applied activity: an inventory of every source of unread employee signal the organization already holds (zero-result search logs, help-desk tickets, all-hands Q&A, help channels, exit and onboarding open text) with owner, obtainability and fidelity; ONE 30-day pilot on one source answering ONE named question; and a charter covering what is collected, what was promised (quoted exactly where a promise exists), who sees it at what grain, the reporting floor, a separate rule for verbatims, what is prohibited outright, and which of the four regimes from Lesson 4 they have NOT checked.

Score at full credit, not as gaps: a source the learner cannot obtain because another function controls it, named with the blocker; a promise they went and read that turns out not to cover what they did; and an explicit list of regimes they have not checked. Naming what has not been checked is worth more than asserting compliance that cannot be demonstrated, and this rubric should say so in feedback.

The pilot must answer ONE question, not deliver a capability. 'Understand employee sentiment' is a capability and should be sent back in feedback; 'which three things did people search for and fail to find after the benefits announcement' is a question. Look for a stated action — what they will do with the answer — because a pilot with no decision attached is instrumentation for its own sake.

A charter with no reporting floor, or with a floor the learner describes as waivable on request, has missed the module's central control. A floor that can be waived when the finding is interesting is not a floor.

Do not require legal conclusions. This module is counsel-gated and the learner is not counsel. Reward correctly identifying WHICH regime applies and what question to ask; do not reward confident assertions that something is lawful.

This track scores the delta rather than the score. Grade the learner's ACCOUNT of the gap between the number of signal sources they predicted and the number they found — direction, size, and what it reveals. NEVER grade prediction accuracy. Finding far more sources than expected is the module working.

opening.label: Predicted — distinct sources of unread employee signal your organization already holds
opening.hint: Things nobody has analyzed. Not surveys you already report on.

calibration.label: Found — how many the inventory actually turned up
calibration.hint: Include the ones you can't currently get, and note who blocks them.

dimensions.name: The inventory is real and includes what can't be reached
dimensions.criteria: Named sources with the system owner, whether it is obtainable this quarter, and a judgement on fidelity. Sources blocked by another function must be included with the blocker named — that is a finding that identifies a conversation to have, not an omission. A generic list that could describe any organization has not been done.

dimensions.name: The pilot answers one question and has an action attached
dimensions.criteria: A single named question rather than a capability, on one source, with what the learner will do with the answer and who sees it. 'Understand employee sentiment' fails; 'which three things did people search for and not find after the benefits announcement, and what we will fix' passes. A pilot with no decision attached is instrumentation for its own sake and should be named as such.

dimensions.name: The charter binds use to the promise
dimensions.criteria: What is collected, what was promised — quoted exactly where a promise exists, or explicitly noted as absent — who sees it at what grain, and what is prohibited outright. The strongest submissions quote the actual privacy note rather than paraphrasing its intent, because the module's rule is that the promise governs, and paraphrase is how promises get quietly widened.

dimensions.name: The floor exists, is unwaivable, and verbatims have their own rule
dimensions.criteria: A minimum cell size set in advance, described as applying without exception, plus a separate rule for free text — since a verbatim referencing a specific project or meeting identifies someone regardless of sample size. A floor the learner describes as waivable on request, or a charter with a count floor and no verbatim rule, has missed the central control.

dimensions.name: Unchecked regimes are named, and the position engages the hardest case
dimensions.criteria: An explicit statement of which of the four regimes — data protection, works councils, monitoring notice, §7 — have not been checked, scored at full credit. Plus a committed position on the claim, engaging the strongest case against it: that the promise was boilerplate nobody authored or relied on, and — sharper — that the promise-based rule systematically protects the powerful, because the patterns a reporting floor suppresses are concentrated in small teams, which is exactly where a bad manager's effects show up. The strongest submissions say what they would actually do with a small-team signal suggesting harm. 'The floor forbids it' is a policy, not an answer.
